# Identity Lifecycle & Access Review Standard

## 1. Purpose

This Standard establishes the requirements for identity lifecycle management, account management, access enforcement, and periodic access review at Example Org. It defines the controls that IAM Engineering must implement, operate, and evidence in order to ensure that access to Example Org systems and to electronic protected health information (ePHI) is granted, maintained, reviewed, and revoked in a controlled and auditable manner.

## 2. Scope

This Standard applies to all Example Org information systems, accounts (including privileged, non-privileged, shared, group, temporary, and emergency accounts), and to all personnel, contractors, and non-organizational users who are granted logical or physical access to those systems. It applies to systems that create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI, and to all identity and access data held in the [Identity Provider].

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

IAM Engineering owns the identity lifecycle and access review process end to end, including account provisioning, deprovisioning, privileged access administration, periodic access certification, and the retention of associated evidence. IAM Engineering is accountable for the outcomes of this process and for coordinating handoffs with HR, supervisors/sponsors, incident response, and other participating teams described below. Other teams (e.g., HR, supervisors, application owners) participate in individual steps of the process but do not own it.

## 4. Policy and Procedure Governance

- Example Org must develop, document, and disseminate an access control policy (addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines) and associated procedures to personnel or roles defined by the organization; designate an official to manage development, documentation, and dissemination of this policy and procedures; and review and update the policy and procedures on an organization-defined frequency (at least every 1 year for AE Mandatory) and following organization-defined events (e.g., assessment/audit findings, security or privacy incidents, or changes in applicable laws/regulations/policies). [NIST AC-1 | ARC-AMPE AC-1 AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must implement policies and procedures ensuring workforce members have appropriate access to electronic PHI and preventing those without authorized access from obtaining it, including procedures for authorization and/or supervision of workforce members, a workforce clearance procedure to determine appropriateness of access, and termination procedures to remove access when employment or the arrangement ends. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(3)(i) | HIPAA 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(A) | HIPAA 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(B) | HIPAA 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(C)]
- IAM Engineering must implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic PHI consistent with applicable requirements, including access authorization procedures for granting access (e.g., to workstations, transactions, programs, or processes) and procedures to establish, document, review, and modify a user's right of access based on those authorization policies; if a health care clearinghouse is part of a larger organization, it must implement policies and procedures protecting its electronic PHI from unauthorized access by the larger organization. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(4)(i) | HIPAA 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(A) | HIPAA 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(B) | HIPAA 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(C)]

## 5. Account Management

- IAM Engineering must define and document the types of accounts allowed and specifically prohibited for use within the system, assign account managers, require organization-defined prerequisites and criteria for group and role membership, specify authorized users, group/role membership, and access authorizations (and any additional organization-defined attributes) for each account, require approvals by organization-defined personnel or roles for account creation requests, create/enable/modify/disable/remove accounts per organization-defined policy and criteria, monitor account use, authorize access based on valid access authorization, intended system usage, and other organization-defined attributes, and align account management processes with personnel termination and transfer processes. [NIST AC-2 | ARC-AMPE AC-2 AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must notify account managers and organization-defined personnel or roles within an organization-defined time period (24 hours for AE Mandatory) when accounts are no longer required, within an organization-defined time period (8 hours for AE Mandatory) when users are terminated or transferred, and within an organization-defined time period (8 hours for AE Mandatory) when system usage or need-to-know changes for an individual. [NIST AC-2 | ARC-AMPE AC-2 AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must review accounts for compliance with account management requirements on an organization-defined frequency (at least every 90 days for all systems for AE Mandatory), and must establish and implement a process for changing shared or group account authenticators, if deployed, when individuals are removed from the group. [NIST AC-2 | ARC-AMPE AC-2 AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must support management of system accounts using automated mechanisms. [NIST AC-2(1) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(1) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must automatically remove or disable temporary and emergency accounts after an organization-defined time period (no more than 96 hours from last use for AE Mandatory). [NIST AC-2(2) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(2) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must disable accounts (non-consumer accounts within 24 hours for AE Mandatory) that have expired, are no longer associated with a user or individual, are in violation of organizational policy, or have been inactive for an organization-defined time period (60 days for AE Mandatory). [NIST AC-2(3) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(3) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must automatically audit account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions. [NIST AC-2(4) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(4) AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must require that users log out when an organization-defined time period of expected inactivity is reached or when a described condition occurs (exceeding 24 hours for AE Mandatory, implemented as a user-policy requirement rather than an automated control). [NIST AC-2(5) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(5) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must establish and administer privileged user accounts in accordance with a role-based (or, per NIST, optionally attribute-based) access scheme, monitor privileged role or attribute assignments and changes to roles or attributes, and revoke access when privileged role or attribute assignments are no longer appropriate; for AE Mandatory, this extends to application-specific privileged accounts, and administrator groups, root accounts, and other system-related accounts must be inspected on demand and at least every 14 days, with application-related privileged roles inspected every 30 days. [NIST AC-2(7) | ARC-AMPE AC-2(7) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must only permit the use of shared and group accounts that meet organization-defined conditions (for AE Mandatory: a documented, AO-approved business need in advance, and a system security plan describing account use with compensating processes for unique attribution of account user activities). [NIST AC-2(9) | ARC-AMPE AC-2(9) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must monitor system accounts for atypical usage and report atypical usage to organization-defined personnel or roles (and, for AE Mandatory, to applicable incident response teams if necessary). [NIST AC-2(12) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(12) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must disable accounts of individuals within an organization-defined time period (1 hour for AE Mandatory) of discovery that the individual poses a significant risk. [NIST AC-2(13) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(13) AE Mandatory]

## 6. Access Enforcement and Authorization

- Example Org must enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies. [NIST AC-3 | ARC-AMPE AC-3 AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must enforce the revocation of access authorizations resulting from changes to the security attributes of subjects and objects based on organization-defined rules (including rules governing the timing of revocations, per AE Mandatory). [NIST AC-3(8) | ARC-AMPE AC-3(8) AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must release information outside the system only if the receiving system, component, or external organization provides organization-defined controls (or, for AE Mandatory, information security and privacy safeguards commensurate with those implemented by the organization), and organization-defined controls are used to validate the appropriateness of the information designated for release. [NIST AC-3(9) | ARC-AMPE AC-3(9) AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must provide organization-defined mechanisms to enable individuals to have access to organization-defined elements of their personally identifiable information (for AE Mandatory, PII/PHI elements defined in applicable security/privacy plans). [NIST AC-3(14) | ARC-AMPE AC-3(14) AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems maintaining electronic PHI to allow access only to persons or software programs granted access rights, including assigning a unique name and/or number to identify and track each user's identity, establishing (and implementing as needed) emergency access procedures, implementing automatic logoff after a predetermined period of inactivity, and implementing a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic PHI. [HIPAA 164.312(a)(1) | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(i) | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(ii) | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iii) | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv)]
- Example Org must implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic PHI is the one claimed. [HIPAA 164.312(d)]

## 7. Separation of Duties and Least Privilege

- IAM Engineering must identify and document organization-defined duties of individuals requiring separation, and define system access authorizations to support separation of duties. [NIST AC-5 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-5 AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) that are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks. [NIST AC-6 Moderate/High | FedRAMP AC-6 | ARC-AMPE AC-6 AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must authorize access to organization-defined security functions (deployed in hardware, software, and firmware) and organization-defined security-relevant information (for FedRAMP: all functions not publicly accessible and all security-relevant information not publicly available; for AE Mandatory: including setting/modifying audit logs and auditing behavior, boundary protection rules, access authorizations, authentication parameters, and system configurations/parameters). [NIST AC-6(1) Moderate/High | FedRAMP AC-6(1) | ARC-AMPE AC-6(1) AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must require that users of accounts or roles with access to organization-defined security functions or security-relevant information (for FedRAMP: all security functions) use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing nonsecurity functions. [NIST AC-6(2) Moderate/High | FedRAMP AC-6(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-6(2) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must restrict privileged accounts on the system to organization-defined personnel or roles. [NIST AC-6(5) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(5) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must review the privileges assigned to organization-defined roles and classes (all users with privileges, at least every 90 days, for AE Mandatory) to validate the need for such privileges, and reassign or remove privileges as necessary to correctly reflect organizational mission and business needs. [NIST AC-6(7) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(7) AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must prevent organization-defined software (for FedRAMP: any software except software explicitly documented) from executing at higher privilege levels than the users executing the software. [NIST AC-6(8) | FedRAMP AC-6(8)]
- Example Org must log the execution of privileged functions. [NIST AC-6(9) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(9) AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions. [NIST AC-6(10) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(10) AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must identify organization-defined user actions that can be performed on the system without identification or authentication, consistent with organizational mission and business functions, and document and provide supporting rationale in the system security plan for user actions not requiring identification or authentication. [NIST AC-14 | ARC-AMPE AC-14 AE Mandatory]

## 8. Identity Management, Identification, and Authentication

- IAM Engineering must manage system identifiers by receiving authorization from organization-defined personnel or roles to assign an individual, group, role, service, or device identifier; selecting an identifier that identifies the individual, group, role, service, or device; assigning the identifier to the intended individual, group, role, service, or device; and preventing reuse of identifiers for an organization-defined time period (2 years for AE Mandatory, including removal of previous identifier-based access authorizations before reuse). [NIST IA-4 | FedRAMP IA-4 | ARC-AMPE IA-4 AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must manage individual identifiers by uniquely identifying each individual according to organization-defined characteristics identifying individual status (for FedRAMP: contractors and foreign nationals; for AE Mandatory: characteristics such as contractors, foreign nationals, or non-organizational users, as defined in applicable security/privacy plans). [NIST IA-4(4) Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-4(4) | ARC-AMPE IA-4(4) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must identity-proof users who require accounts for logical access to systems based on appropriate identity assurance level requirements specified in applicable standards and guidelines, resolve user identities to a unique individual, and collect, validate, and verify identity evidence (for AE Mandatory, this applies to all accounts including non-privileged/consumer accounts, and users must be proofed to Identity Assurance Level 2 (IAL-2) or higher per NIST SP 800-63, or via the Federal Data Services Hub Remote Identity Proofing Service for ACA Consumer Accounts). [NIST IA-12 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-12 AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must require that the registration process to receive an account for logical access include supervisor or sponsor authorization (for AE Mandatory, required for all accounts including non-privileged/consumer accounts). [NIST IA-12(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-12(1) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must require that evidence of individual identification be presented to the registration authority (for AE Mandatory, required for all accounts including non-privileged/consumer accounts). [NIST IA-12(2) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-12(2) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must require that presented identity evidence be validated and verified through organization-defined (or organization-approved, for AE Mandatory, and CMS-agreement-compliant) methods of validation and verification, applying to all accounts including non-privileged/consumer accounts for AE Mandatory. [NIST IA-12(3) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-12(3) AE Mandatory]

## 9. Personnel Transfer and Termination

- Upon termination of individual employment, IAM Engineering must disable system access within an organization-defined time period (the same day as termination for AE Mandatory), terminate or revoke any authenticators and credentials associated with the individual, conduct exit interviews covering organization-defined information security topics (including non-disclosure of information security and privacy information for AE Mandatory), retrieve all security-related organizational system-related property, and retain access to organizational information and systems formerly controlled by the terminated individual. [NIST PS-4 | ARC-AMPE PS-4 AE Mandatory]
- When individuals are reassigned or transferred to other positions within the organization, IAM Engineering must review and confirm ongoing operational need for current logical and physical access authorizations to systems and facilities, initiate organization-defined transfer or reassignment actions within an organization-defined time period following the formal transfer action (for AE Mandatory, ensuring all no-longer-required system accesses are removed or disabled within 24 hours), modify access authorization as needed to correspond with changes in operational need, and notify organization-defined personnel or roles within an organization-defined time period (24 hours for AE Mandatory). [NIST PS-5 | ARC-AMPE PS-5 AE Mandatory]

## 10. Workstation Environment Controls

- Example Org must implement policies and procedures specifying the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic PHI. [HIPAA 164.310(b)]

## 11. Documentation and Records Retention

- IAM Engineering must maintain access-related policies and procedures, and records of required actions, activities, or assessments, in written (which may be electronic) form; retain such documentation for 6 years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later; make it available to those responsible for implementing the procedures; and review and update it periodically in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic PHI. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(1) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]

## 12. Quarterly Identity Lifecycle & Access Review Process

IAM Engineering must conduct the identity lifecycle and access review process described in this Standard on a quarterly basis. Each quarterly cycle must, at a minimum, satisfy the account-review and privileged-access-review floors set out in Sections 5 and 7 above (e.g., the at-least-every-90-days review requirement under [NIST AC-2 | ARC-AMPE AC-2 AE Mandatory] and [NIST AC-6(7) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(7) AE Mandatory]).

For each quarterly cycle, IAM Engineering must produce and retain the following evidence, consistent with the retention requirements in Section 11:

| Evidence Artifact                   | Source / System     | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Identity provider user export       | [Identity Provider] | Establishes the authoritative list of active accounts and associated attributes for the review cycle.                                                                                                                                                       |
| HR active-employee roster           | HR system of record | Establishes the authoritative list of currently employed/engaged individuals, used to reconcile against active accounts and identify accounts requiring disablement per Sections 5 and 9.                                                                   |
| Access review tickets with sign-off | [Ticketing System]  | Records the review decision, approver, and remediation action for each account or privilege identified during the review, providing the auditable trail of account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions described in Section 5. |

IAM Engineering must reconcile the identity provider user export against the HR active-employee roster during each quarterly cycle, open an access review ticket in the [Ticketing System] for any discrepancy (including accounts of individuals no longer on the HR roster, dormant accounts, or privileged accounts lacking a validated business need), and obtain documented sign-off in the [Ticketing System] before closing each ticket. These sign-off records constitute the evidence of compliance with the account review, privileged access review, and access authorization modification requirements referenced throughout this Standard.
